title: Light-Hole Spin Qubits in Strained SiGe Lattice-Matched to Ge
authors: Edmondo Valvo, Davide Costa, Patrick Del Vecchio, Stefano Bosco, Giordano Scappucci, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ
abstract: Strained germanium ($\varepsilon$-Ge) quantum wells on metamorphic SiGe buffers have enabled advanced hole-based spin qubit devices. Alternatively, unstrained Ge with lattice-matched strained silicon-germanium ($\varepsilon$-SiGe) barriers eliminates the need for metamorphic buffers altogether. The ground state character of both these platforms is predominantly heavy-hole (HH) with a largely anisotropic spin response. We propose and study an alternative heterostructure, lattice-matched to Ge, in which both the SiGe quantum well and barriers are tensile strained, with their composition contrast providing the band offset for confinement and the tensile strain stabilizing a light-hole (LH) ground state. We show large spin-orbit coupling (SOC), both linear and cubic, along with a significantly more isotropic spin response compared to strained HH qubits. We also study the decoherence properties of the proposed device, showing an appreciable gain in the quality factor compared to their HH counterparts. Finally, we propose a bilayer heterostructure that allows for electrical switching between HH and LH ground state character.
summary: This theoretical work proposes using tensile-strained SiGe/Ge heterostructures to create light-hole (LH) spin qubits, overcoming limitations found in conventional heavy-hole (HH) qubits. By engineering the lattice structure, the authors achieve a significantly more isotropic spin response and a substantial increase in the qubit's quality factor. The model also demonstrates the feasibility of electrically switching between HH and LH ground states.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for advanced hole-based spin qubits with improved coherence and reduced spin anisotropy compared to established heavy-hole (HH) platforms.
main_result: The proposed tensile-strained Light-Hole (LH) heterostructure lattice-matched to Ge successfully stabilizes an LH ground state exhibiting large spin-orbit coupling and an order-of-magnitude improvement in the quality factor.
method: The study employs theoretical calculations involving the numerical diagonalization of a 6-band k.p Hamiltonian and projecting the resulting Hamiltonian to analyze spin properties.
model_or_system: The physical system is a quantum well/barrier structure made of tensile-strained SiGe/Ge, designed to confine holes in a light-hole (LH) ground state. The model uses a k.p Hamiltonian incorporating linear and cubic spin-orbit coupling terms.
key_observables: Spin-orbit coupling parameters ($\alpha,  eta_2,  eta_3$), g-tensor components ($g^*_{\parallel}, g^*_{\perp}$), dipole moment, and Quality factor ($Q$).
important_parameters: Well thickness ($L_z$), Ge concentration ($x_w$), and applied electric field ($F_z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system remains structurally stable against strain relaxation, and calculations are performed by projecting the full Hamiltonian onto the LH ground state doublet.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy gap closure between HH and LH states, the dependence of SOC parameters and effective mass on composition/thickness, and the tunability of the g-tensor components with applied electric fields.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the proposed LH platform against traditional HH platforms, deriving the effective Hamiltonian, calculating key spin parameters (SOC, g-tensor), and demonstrating the advantages in coherence and tunability, culminating in the proposal of a switching bilayer structure.
why_interesting: The detailed theoretical modeling of spin-orbit coupling and g-tensor renormalization in semiconductor heterostructures is highly relevant for designing solid-state qubits, providing concrete material parameters for quantum device engineering.
